proofs.proof_tex:
Let \(K=\lceil8\log(2d/\alpha)\rceil\), \(q=\lfloor n/K\rfloor\), and \(\rho=\sqrt{8V_\psi/q}\) as in Definition \(\mathrm{def:chart\text{-}moment\text{-}rule}\).  Write
\[
\mu_j=\mathbb E_P\psi(X_j,Y_j)=\theta_j2t_j(1-2a_j).
\]
By Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:subhalf\text{-}chart\text{-}calibration}\), each block mean has variance at most \(V_\psi/q\).  Chebyshev's inequality therefore makes the probability that a specified block mean differs from \(\mu_j\) by more than \(\rho\) at most \(1/8\).  The \(K\) block means are independent because the observations are independent.  If their median differs from \(\mu_j\) by more than \(\rho\), at least \(K/2\) blocks are bad.  A union bound over subsets of bad blocks gives
\[
P^{\otimes n}(|\widehat\mu_j-\mu_j|>\rho)
\le2^K(1/8)^{K/2}=2^{-K/2}
\le\frac{\alpha}{2d}.
\]
The last inequality uses \(K\ge8\log(2d/\alpha)\) and \(4\log2>1\).  A union bound over \(j\in I\) shows that
\[
\mathcal E=\left\{\max_{j\in I}|\widehat\mu_j-\mu_j|\le\rho\right\}
\]
has probability at least \(1-\alpha/2\), uniformly over the chart class.

Because \(a_j\le a_+<1/2\), the moment sign is the causal orientation: \(\operatorname{sign}(\mu_j)=\theta_j\).  Also the residual margin and the upper HSIC comparison in the calibration lemma imply
\[
t_j^2\ge\lambda/C_H,
\qquad
|\mu_j|^2\ge4(1-2a_+)^2\lambda/C_H.
\]
When \(n\ge2K\), \(q\ge n/(2K)\), and hence
\[
\rho^2\le\frac{16V_\psi K}{n}.
\]
Since \(\log(2d/\alpha)\) and \(\log((d+1)/\alpha)\) differ by universal factors and \(K\le9\log(2d/\alpha)\), increasing a constant \(C\) depending only on \(V_\psi,C_H\), and \(1-2a_+\) makes
\[
n\lambda\ge C\log\frac{d+1}{\alpha}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
2\rho<\min_{j\in I}|\mu_j|.
\]
This same inequality implies \(n\ge2K\) because \(\lambda\le1\).  On \(\mathcal E\), each interval \([\widehat\mu_j-\rho,\widehat\mu_j+\rho]\) then lies strictly in the half-line with sign \(\theta_j\).  Thus \(B_j=\{\theta_j\}\) for all \(j\), \(\widehat{\mathcal C}_n^{\mathrm H}=\{\theta\}\), and \(\widehat\theta_n^{\mathrm H}=\theta\).  The asserted upper error bound follows.

Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:chart\text{-}product\text{-}testing\text{-}lower}\) supplies the lower bound for every measurable procedure on the identical class.  Applying Definition \(\mathrm{def:chart\text{-}minimax\text{-}frontier}\) proves the displayed two-sided bound; integer ceilings are absorbed because \(\log((d+1)/\alpha)\ge\log8\).  Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:product\text{-}testing\text{-}converse}\) independently supplies the asserted lower bound for the full-class functional \(N^*\).  Equivalently, the inclusion \(\mathcal M_d^{\mathrm H}(\lambda)\subset\mathcal M_d(\lambda)\) in Definition \(\mathrm{def:subhalf\text{-}hermite\text{-}class}\) shows directly that taking a supremum over the larger class can only increase minimax risk.

For completeness, let \(\mathcal P_d^{\mathrm{Pet}}\) denote Peters et al.'s positive-density restricted-ANM class on a DAG consisting of \(d\) disjoint directed edges.  Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:peters\text{-}disjoint\text{-}pair\text{-}specialization}\) and the eight member conditions in Definition \(\mathrm{def:base\text{-}model}\) give
\[
\mathcal M_d^{\mathrm H}(\lambda)\subset\mathcal M_d(\lambda)
\subset\mathcal P_d^{\mathrm{Pet}}.
\]
The latter inclusion is strict: apply a common nonunit affine rescaling to every coordinate of any positive chart law.  Affine rescaling preserves positivity, the additive-noise equation, exogeneity, and restrictedness, but violates the unit-variance properties imposed by \(\mathcal M_d(\lambda)\).  Hence the chart converse, like Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:product\text{-}testing\text{-}converse}\), transfers upward to the corresponding larger published class.  No reverse transfer is used for achievability.

All block boundaries, block averages, lower medians, interval endpoints, Cartesian products, and fallback choices in Definition \(\mathrm{def:chart\text{-}moment\text{-}rule}\) are deterministic Borel operations on the sample, so the set is measurable.  One evaluation of \(\psi\) is made for each of the \(nd\) observed pairs; block summation and medians add \(O(dn)\) arithmetic work and require exactly \(d\) coordinatewise moment queries.

The event \(\mathcal E\) constructed in the proof of Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:uniform\text{-}minimax\text{-}frontier}\) has probability at least \(1-\alpha/2\).  On it, the interval centered at \(\widehat\mu_j\) contains \(\mu_j\).  Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:subhalf\text{-}chart\text{-}calibration}\) gives
\[
\operatorname{sign}(\mu_j)=\theta_j,
\]
so the half-line for \(\theta_j\) intersects that interval and \(\theta_j\in B_j\).  Hence \(\theta\in\prod_jB_j=\widehat{\mathcal C}_n^{\mathrm H}\), which proves coverage.  Notice that Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:population\text{-}direction\text{-}margin}\) independently gives \(H_{j,\theta_j}=0<H_{j,-\theta_j}\); thus the moment sign estimates the same causal orientation identified by residual HSIC, rather than defining a new target.

Under the displayed signal inequality, the radius calculation in the proof of Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:uniform\text{-}minimax\text{-}frontier}\) gives \(2\rho<|\mu_j|\) for every \(j\).  On \(\mathcal E\) the whole interval then has sign \(\theta_j\), so \(B_j=\{\theta_j\}\) for all \(j\).  This proves the singleton guarantee.  The final assertion is exactly the random-set part of Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:chart\text{-}product\text{-}testing\text{-}lower}\), on the identical chart class and with the identical confidence level.

For \(d=1\), the Cartesian product over \(I=\{1\}\) is \(B_1\) itself.  Substituting \(d=1\) into Definition \(\mathrm{def:chart\text{-}moment\text{-}rule}\) gives exactly the two displayed half-line intersection conditions.  Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:subhalf\text{-}chart\text{-}calibration}\) gives
\[
\mathbb E\psi(X_1,Y_1)=\theta_1,2t_1(1-2a_1),
\]
whose sign is \(\theta_1\) because \(t_1>0\) and \(a_1<1/2\).  Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:population\text{-}direction\text{-}margin}\) gives \(H_{1,\theta_1}=0<H_{1,-\theta_1}\), proving that this sign rule targets the same identified causal direction.  Specializing the two inequalities in Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:uniform\text{-}minimax\text{-}frontier}\) to \(d=1\) yields
\[
c\lambda^{-1}\log(2/\alpha)
\le N_{\mathrm H}^*(1,\alpha,\lambda)
\le C\lambda^{-1}\log(2/\alpha),
\]
with constants independent of \(\alpha\) and \(\lambda\) on \((0,1/4]\times(0,\lambda_H]\).

Choose a fixed nonlinear chart member \(P^\circ=P_{a,t,+}\) supplied by Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:attainable\text{-}margin\text{-}rectangle}\), with \(a\) in the interior of its compact interval and fixed \(t\in(0,t_0]\).  For the true-direction query,
\[
C=Z\sim\mathcal N(0,1),
\qquad
m(z)=az+t(z^2-1).
\]
Fix one of the four regression folds and let its size be \(m_n\), so \(m_n/n\to1/4\); put \(h=h_n\).  Choose \(0<\delta<1-\log2\), which implies \(e^{-\delta}>2e^{-1}\).  For all sufficiently large \(n\), continuity and strict monotonicity of the Gaussian upper tail give a number \(z_n>0\) such that, with
\[
J_n=[z_n-2h,z_n+2h],
\qquad
m_nP^\circ(Z\in J_n)=\delta.
\]
Let \(\varphi_0\) be the standard-normal density.  Since \(nh\to\infty\), the required interval probability tends to zero and hence \(z_n\to\infty\).  The mean-value theorem gives
\[
P(Z\in J_n)=4h\varphi_0(\zeta_n)
\]
for some \(\zeta_n\in J_n\).  Solving this equality, using \(m_n\asymp n\) and \(h=n^{-1/(2\beta+1)}\) up to fixed factors, first yields \(z_n=O(\sqrt{\log n})\); consequently \(z_nh\to0\) and \(\zeta_n^2-z_n^2=o(1)\).  Taking logarithms now gives
\[
z_n^2=\frac{4\beta}{2\beta+1}\log n+O(\log\log n).
\]
Because \(4\beta/(2\beta+1)<2\), whereas \(T_n^2=8\log(n\vee3)/c_0\) and \(c_0<1\), we have \(z_n<T_n-h\) for all sufficiently large \(n\).

Set \(A_n=[z_n-h/2,z_n+h/2]\).  Since the Gaussian density ratio over \(J_n\) is bounded between \(e^{-4z_nh-8h^2}\) and \(e^{4z_nh+8h^2}\), it tends uniformly to one.  The ratio of the lengths of \(A_n\) and \(J_n\) is \(1/4\), so
\[
P^\circ(Z\in A_n)\ge c/n
\]
for a fixed \(c>0\) and all large \(n\).

Let \(E_n\) be the event that the selected regression fold contains no predictor in \(J_n\).  Independence of observations and the defining equality for \(J_n\) give
\[
P^{\circ\otimes n}(E_n)
=\left(1-\frac\delta{m_n}\right)^{m_n}\longrightarrow e^{-\delta}.
\]
For every \(z\in A_n\), the support condition \(|(Z_i-z)/h|\le1\) implies \(Z_i\in J_n\).  Thus, on \(E_n\), every weighted least-squares term in Definition \(\mathrm{def:admissible\text{-}local\text{-}polynomial\text{-}class}\) is zero.  Its positive ridge term makes the unique coefficient vector zero, and clipping leaves \(\widehat m(z)=0\) throughout \(A_n\).  Since \(t>0\) is fixed and \(z_n\to\infty\),
\[
\inf_{z\in A_n}|m(z)|\ge c_1z_n^2\ge c_2\log n.
\]
Therefore, on \(E_n\),
\[
\|\widehat m-m\|_{L^4(P_C)}
\ge\left\{\int_{A_n}|m(z)|^4\,dP_C(z)\right\}^{1/4}
\ge c_3n^{-1/4}\log n.
\]
The strict smoothness condition \(\beta>1/2\) is exactly
\[
\frac{\beta}{2\beta+1}>\frac14.
\]
Hence
\[
r_n+\sqrt{(1+\log2)/n}
=o(n^{-1/4}\log n).
\]
For every fixed finite \(C_m>0\), the event \(E_n\) is therefore contained, for all sufficiently large \(n\), in the complement of \(\mathcal G_n(1;C_m,\widehat m)\).  The maximum over rotations and queries in that event only strengthens this inclusion.  Taking lower limits proves
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}P^{\circ\otimes n}\{\mathcal G_n(1;C_m,\widehat m)^c\}
\ge e^{-\delta}>2e^{-1}.
\]
The requested generated-residual expansion required the regression event itself with complement probability at most \(2e^{-1}\).  Because this necessary event already fails, no subsequent measurable orthogonalization or data-dependent radius constructed through \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{orth}}(\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{LP}})\) can satisfy that assertion.  This conclusion is only an obstruction for the fixed local-polynomial \(L^4\) protocol; it is not an upper or lower bound on residual-HSIC estimation error.

added_lemmas.statement:
The existential chart constants in Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:attainable\text{-}margin\text{-}rectangle}\) may be selected with \(0<a_-<a_+<1/2\).  For such a selection there are \(t_\star>0\), \(0<\lambda_H\le\lambda_0\), and constants \(0<c_H<C_H<\infty\) such that every \((P_{a,t,\theta},\theta)\in\mathcal M_d^{\mathrm H}(\lambda)\) satisfies, for every \(j\in I\),
\[
\mathbb E_{P_{a,t,\theta}}\psi(X_j,Y_j)=\theta_j\,2t_j(1-2a_j),
\qquad
\operatorname{Var}_{P_{a,t,\theta}}\{\psi(X_j,Y_j)\}\le V_\psi,
\]
and
\[
c_Ht_j^2\le H_{j,-\theta_j}(P_{a,t,\theta})\le C_Ht_j^2.
\]
The class \(\mathcal M_d^{\mathrm H}(\lambda)\) is nonempty for every \(d\ge1\) and \(0<\lambda\le\lambda_H\).  More precisely, there are \(a_0\in(a_-,a_+)\), a continuous choice \(t_\lambda\in(0,t_\star]\), and \(C_I<\infty\) such that \(H_{1,-}(P_{a_0,t_\lambda,+})=\lambda\), both coordinate-swapped orientations belong to \(\mathcal M_1^{\mathrm H}(\lambda)\), and
\[
\operatorname{KL}(P_{a_0,t_\lambda,+}\Vert P_{a_0,t_\lambda,-})\le C_I\lambda.
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Choose, for example, a compact interval \(A=[1/8,1/4]\subset(0,1/2)\).  The chart membership calculation underlying the already-proved Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:attainable\text{-}margin\text{-}rectangle}\) is uniform on every compact subset of \((0,1)\): for \(a\in A\) and sufficiently small positive \(t\),
\[
C=Z,\qquad E=aZ+t(Z^2-1)+s_{a,t}\xi,qquad
s_{a,t}^2=1-a^2-2t^2,
\]
with independent standard normal \(Z,\xi\).  Taking \(t_\star\) small makes \(s_{a,t}^2\) uniformly bounded away from zero.  The cause and noise densities are then everywhere positive Gaussian densities, \(C\perp\xi\), and the product construction gives independent pairs.  Also
\[
\operatorname{Var}(C)=1,qquad
\operatorname{Var}(E)=a^2+2t^2+s_{a,t}^2=1.
\]
The mechanism is quadratic and both log densities are quadratic, so their weighted H\"older norms in \(\mathcal H_{(2)}^\beta(L)\) are uniformly finite after selecting the fixed existential envelope in that theorem.  The same chart calculation verifies Peters et al.'s restricted-ANM Condition 19 for every \(t>0\); the excluded boundary \(t=0\) is exactly the reversible linear-Gaussian member.  Hence all eight properties in Definition \(\mathrm{def:base\text{-}model}\) hold.  The one-sided expansion from Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:attainable\text{-}margin\text{-}rectangle}\) gives, uniformly on \(A\),
\[
H_{j,-\theta_j}=\kappa_H(a_j)t_j^2+O(t_j^3),
\qquad
g_j=\frac{a_j^2}{2}+O(t_j^2).
\]
The Gaussian integral defining \(\kappa_H\) is continuous in \(a\) by dominated convergence, because both kernels are bounded by one and the chart densities have a common Gaussian envelope.  The established positivity of the coefficient therefore yields
\[
0<\kappa_-:=\inf_{a\in A}\kappa_H(a)
\le \sup_{a\in A}\kappa_H(a)=:\kappa_+<\infty.
\]
Decrease \(t_\star\) until the uniform remainder has absolute value at most \(\kappa_-t^2/2\).  Then the asserted HSIC inequalities hold with \(c_H=\kappa_-/2\) and, for example, \(C_H=\kappa_++\kappa_-/2\).  Choose \(\underline g\) strictly below \((1/8)^2/2\) and \(\overline g\) strictly above \((1/4)^2/2\), and decrease \(t_\star\) once more; the gain expansion then gives the navigation window throughout the subchart.

It remains to compute the observable moment.  In the orientation \(\theta_j=+1\), write \(X=Z\) and \(Y=aZ+t(Z^2-1)+s\xi\).  Centering and the standard-normal moments \(\mathbb EZ^2=1\), \(\mathbb EZ^4=3\) give
\[
\mathbb E[(X^2-1)Y]
=t\mathbb E[(Z^2-1)^2]=2t.
\]
Moreover,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E[(Y^2-1)X]
&=\mathbb E[ZY^2]\\
&=2at\,\mathbb E[Z^2(Z^2-1)]
=4at,
\end{aligned}
\]
because every remaining term is an odd centered Gaussian moment or contains the independent centered \(\xi\).  Thus \(\mathbb E\psi(X,Y)=2t(1-2a)\).  Coordinate swapping changes \(\psi(x,y)\) to \(-\psi(x,y)\), proving the formula for both orientations.

For the variance, \(|a|,t,s\le1\) implies
\[
|Y|^8\le3^7\{|Z|^8+|Z^2-1|^8+|\xi|^8\},
\qquad \mathbb E|Y|^8\le M_8.
\]
The elementary inequality \((u^2-1)^2\le2(u^4+1)\), followed by Cauchy--Schwarz and Lyapunov's moment inequality, yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E\psi(X,Y)^2
&\le4\{\mathbb E(X^4Y^2)+\mathbb EY^2+\mathbb E(Y^4X^2)+\mathbb EX^2\}\\
&\le4\left\{(\mathbb E|Z|^8)^{1/2}M_8^{1/4}+2
+M_8^{1/2}(\mathbb E|Z|^4)^{1/2}\right\}=V_\psi.
\end{aligned}
\]
Since variance is at most the second moment, the claimed variance bound follows.

Finally fix \(a_0\in(1/8,1/4)\).  The one-sided Jacobian assertion in Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:attainable\text{-}margin\text{-}rectangle}\), equivalently the expansion with positive coefficient just used, makes \(t^2\mapsto H_{1,-}(P_{a_0,t,+})\) locally invertible at zero.  Hence, after choosing \(\lambda_H>0\) small enough, for each \(0<\lambda\le\lambda_H\) there is \(t_\lambda\le t_\star\) with \(H_{1,-}=\lambda\), and \(t_\lambda^2\asymp\lambda\).  The gain window already proved and \(A_H>1\) put both coordinate-swapped laws in \(\mathcal M_1^{\mathrm H}(\lambda)\).  Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:mirror\text{-}information}\), restricted to the smaller compact interval \(A\), gives
\[
\operatorname{KL}(P_{a_0,t_\lambda,+}\Vert P_{a_0,t_\lambda,-})
\le C_I\lambda.
\]
Taking products of these one-pair members proves nonemptiness for every \(d\).

added_lemmas.statement:
There is a constant \(c_L>0\), depending only on the fixed sub-half chart, such that for every \(d\ge1\), \(0<\alpha\le1/4\), \(0<\lambda\le\lambda_H\), and every measurable estimator \(\widetilde\theta\),
\[
n\lambda\le c_L\log\frac{d+1}{\alpha}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\sup_{(P,\theta)\in\mathcal M_d^{\mathrm H}(\lambda)}
P^{\otimes n}(\widetilde\theta\ne\theta)>\alpha.
\]
In the same regime, no random set can have both uniform coverage at least \(1-\alpha/2\) and uniform singleton probability at least \(1-\alpha/2\) over \(\mathcal M_d^{\mathrm H}(\lambda)\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Let \(Q_\lambda^+=P_{a_0,t_\lambda,+}\) and \(Q_\lambda^-=P_{a_0,t_\lambda,-}\) be the two laws furnished by Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:subhalf\text{-}chart\text{-}calibration}\).  For \(\vartheta\in\{-1,+1\}^d\), form
\[
Q_\vartheta=\bigotimes_{j=1}^d Q_\lambda^{\vartheta_j}.
\]
The product and margin parts of that lemma show \((Q_\vartheta,\vartheta)\in\mathcal M_d^{\mathrm H}(\lambda)\).  Put \(K_n=n\operatorname{KL}(Q_\lambda^+\Vert Q_\lambda^-)\le C_In\lambda\).

We first derive the binary testing bound used below.  For probability measures \(R,S\) with densities \(r,s\), their affinity \(A(R,S)=\int\sqrt{rs}\) satisfies
\[
\operatorname{KL}(R\Vert S)
=-2\mathbb E_R\log\sqrt{s/r}
\ge-2\log A(R,S)
\]
by Jensen's inequality.  Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
\|R-S\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
\le\sqrt{1-A(R,S)^2}.
\]
Applying these inequalities to \(R=(Q_\lambda^+)^{\otimes n}\) and \(S=(Q_\lambda^-)^{\otimes n}\), whose affinity is the \(n\)-th power of the one-observation affinity, shows that the equal-prior binary Bayes error \(e_n\) obeys
\[
e_n=\frac{1-\|R-S\|_{\mathrm{TV}}}{2}
\ge \frac{1-\sqrt{1-e^{-K_n}}}{2}.
\]

Under the uniform prior on \(\vartheta\), both the prior and the likelihood factor over coordinates.  Therefore the Bayes-optimal vector rule is the product of the binary Bayes rules, and its exact-recovery error is \(1-(1-e_n)^d\).  Every estimator consequently has average, and hence worst-case, error at least that quantity.

Set \(\gamma=1/64\) and choose \(c_L<\gamma/C_I\).  If \(R_\alpha=(d+1)/\alpha\) and \(n\lambda\le c_L\log R_\alpha\), then \(e^{-K_n}>R_\alpha^{-\gamma}\).  For \(d\le2\),
\[
R_\alpha^{-\gamma}\ge(3/\alpha)^{-\gamma}>4\alpha(1-\alpha),
\]
where the last inequality follows because the ratio of the left side to the right side is decreasing on \((0,1/4]\) and at \(\alpha=1/4\) equals \(12^{-1/64}/(3/4)>1\).  The displayed binary bound then gives \(e_n>\alpha\).  For \(d\ge3\), the inequality \(1-\sqrt{1-x}\ge x/2\) gives \(e_n>R_\alpha^{-\gamma}/4\).  With \(x=d/\alpha\ge12\) and \(R_\alpha\le(4/3)x\),
\[
de_n>\frac{x\alpha}{4}\{(4/3)x\}^{-\gamma}\ge2\alpha,
\]
because \(x^{1-\gamma}\ge8(4/3)^\gamma\) at \(x=12\) and the left side is increasing in \(x\).  If \(de_n\le1\), then \(1-(1-e_n)^d\ge1-e^{-de_n}\ge de_n/2>\alpha\); if \(de_n>1\), the same quantity exceeds \(1-e^{-1}>1/4\ge\alpha\).  This proves the estimator lower bound.

For the random-set claim, suppose that a set \(\widetilde{\mathcal C}\) had coverage at least \(1-\alpha/2\) and singleton probability at least \(1-\alpha/2\) under every chart law.  Return its unique element on the singleton event and use a fixed fallback otherwise.  For every parameter,
\[
P^{\otimes n}(\widetilde\theta\ne\theta)
\le P^{\otimes n}\{\theta\notin\widetilde{\mathcal C}\}
+P^{\otimes n}\{|\widetilde{\mathcal C}|\ne1\}
\le\alpha,
\]
contradicting the strict estimator lower bound.  Thus the two uniform guarantees cannot coexist.

added_lemmas.statement: For a directed acyclic graph that is a disjoint union of directed edges, the multivariate restricted additive-noise condition in Peters et al.'s Definition 27 specializes to the conjunction of their bivariate Condition 19 over the edges; under that condition their Theorem 28 identifies the directed acyclic graph from the observational law.

attestation.note: The disjoint-edge specialization was supplied explicitly in the orchestrator directive; the stable JMLR carrier is recorded because no verbatim source transcription was supplied.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Fix the sub-half Hermite chart selected in Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:subhalf\text{-}chart\text{-}calibration}\).  There are constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), depending only on this fixed chart and on the fixed Gaussian kernels, such that for every \(d\ge1\), \(0<\alpha\le1/4\), and \(0<\lambda\le\lambda_H\),
\[
n\lambda\ge C\log\frac{d+1}{\alpha}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\sup_{(P,\theta)\in\mathcal M_d^{\mathrm H}(\lambda)}
P^{\otimes n}(\widehat\theta_n^{\mathrm H}\ne\theta)\le\alpha/2,
\]
where \(\widehat\theta_n^{\mathrm H}\) is the explicit median-of-means rule in Definition \(\mathrm{def:chart\text{-}moment\text{-}rule}\).  Every measurable estimator has worst-case error greater than \(\alpha\) when \(n\lambda\le c\log((d+1)/\alpha)\).  Consequently,
\[
c\frac{\log((d+1)/\alpha)}{\lambda}
\le N_{\mathrm H}^*(d,\alpha,\lambda)
\le C\frac{\log((d+1)/\alpha)}{\lambda}.
\]
Since \(\mathcal M_d^{\mathrm H}(\lambda)\subset\mathcal M_d(\lambda)\), the same lower bound transfers to the full-class frontier \(N^*(d,\alpha,\lambda)\), but no full-class upper bound is asserted.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The existing antecedent is false by the proved fixed-local-polynomial obstruction, so its full-class upper bound is vacuous. The replacement narrows the parameter space to the explicit sub-half Hermite chart and proves an unconditional matched all-procedure frontier there.

The generated-residual intervals cannot obtain their asserted full-class event. The replacement narrows to the same explicit chart and uses a computable observable-moment confidence set with a matching singleton obstruction.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
When \(d=1\), Definition \(\mathrm{def:chart\text{-}moment\text{-}rule}\) gives \(\widehat{\mathcal C}_n^{\mathrm H}=B_1\): it contains \(+1\) exactly when \(\widehat\mu_1+\rho_{n,1,\alpha}\ge0\) and contains \(-1\) exactly when \(\widehat\mu_1-\rho_{n,1,\alpha}\le0\).  On the sub-half chart the population sign of \(\mathbb E\psi(X_1,Y_1)\) equals the unique zero-residual-HSIC direction, and
\[
N_{\mathrm H}^*(1,\alpha,\lambda)\asymp
\lambda^{-1}\log(2/\alpha),
\qquad 0<\alpha\le1/4,\quad 0<\lambda\le\lambda_H.
\]
proposed_statement_changes.reason: After replacing the vacuous local-polynomial procedure, the faithful single-pair specialization is the median-of-means sign interval on the chart, related by proof to the same causal residual-HSIC orientation.

proposed.name: GENE-inspired population correcting gain
proposed.construction:
\[
q_{j,b}=\frac{\operatorname{Var}_P\{m_{j,b}(C_{j,b})\}}{\operatorname{Var}_P(E_{j,b})},\qquad
s_{j,b}=q_{j,b}\left(1-\frac12\mathbf 1\{H_{j,b}>0\}\right),\qquad
g_j=s_{j,\theta_j}-s_{j,-\theta_j}.
\]
This is a GENE-inspired population score: its independence coordinate is the oracle indicator \(\mathbf 1\{H_{j,b}>0\}\) for fixed characteristic Gaussian-kernel HSIC.  It is not the published GENE score, which uses a discretized chi-square independence-test indicator together with neural-network \(R^2\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: Li et al.'s published GENE uses neural-network explained variance and a discretized chi-square test indicator; this definition instead uses population explained variance and the oracle indicator of positive fixed-kernel HSIC.
The map's name must inherit the corrected score attribution.

proposed.name: separated sub-half Hermite-chart experiment
proposed.construction:
Fix constants \(0<a_-<a_+<1/2\), \(t_\star>0\), and \(0<\lambda_H\le\lambda_0\).  For \(0<\lambda\le\lambda_H\), define
\[
\mathcal M_d^{\mathrm H}(\lambda)
=\left\{(P_{a,t,\theta},\theta):
\begin{array}{l}
\theta\in\{-1,+1\}^{I},\ a\in[a_-,a_+]^d,\ 0<t_j\le t_\star\ (j\in I),\\
(P_{a,t,\theta},\theta)\text{ is the law--orientation projection of a member of }\mathcal M_d(\lambda)
\end{array}
\right\}.
\]
Thus \(\mathcal M_d^{\mathrm H}(\lambda)\) is an explicitly parameterized subclass of the separated positive-density restricted-ANM experiment; membership still requires every law property in \(\mathcal M_d(\lambda)\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: This is the explicit identical subclass on which both the moment upper bound and product-testing converse hold.

proposed.name: antisymmetric chart moment
proposed.construction:
For one labelled pair define the antisymmetric observable
\[
\psi(x,y)=(x^2-1)y-(y^2-1)x.
\]
For observation \(W_i\) and pair \(j\), write \(\psi_{ij}=\psi(X_j(W_i),Y_j(W_i))\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The observable has expectation proportional to the signed nonlinear chart coordinate and needs no regression nuisance.

proposed.name: computable chart-moment variance envelope
proposed.construction:
Let \(Z\sim\mathcal N(0,1)\), put
\[
M_8=3^7\left(2\mathbb E|Z|^8+\mathbb E|Z^2-1|^8\right),
\]
and define the computable constant
\[
V_\psi=4\left\{(\mathbb E|Z|^8)^{1/2}M_8^{1/4}+2+M_8^{1/2}(\mathbb E|Z|^4)^{1/2}\right\}.
\]
All Gaussian moments in this display are explicit integers or finite sums of explicit integers.

proposed_core_edits.reason: A known finite constant makes the confidence radius explicit and uniform over the compact chart.

proposed.name: median-of-means chart orientation rule and confidence set
proposed.construction:
Let
\[
K=\left\lceil 8\log\frac{2d}{\alpha}\right\rceil,
\qquad q=\left\lfloor\frac nK\right\rfloor,
\qquad \rho_{n,d,\alpha}=\sqrt{\frac{8V_\psi}{q}},
\]
and suppose \(n\ge2K\).  Partition the first \(Kq\) observation indices deterministically into \(K\) consecutive blocks \(A_1,\ldots,A_K\) of size \(q\).  For each \(j\in I\), set
\[
\widehat\mu_j=\operatorname{Med}_{1\le k\le K}
\left\{q^{-1}\sum_{i\in A_k}\psi_{ij}\right\},
\]
using the lower median when \(K\) is even, and form
\[
B_j=\{+1:\widehat\mu_j+\rho_{n,d,\alpha}\ge0\}
\cup\{-1:\widehat\mu_j-\rho_{n,d,\alpha}\le0\}.
\]
Set \(\widehat{\mathcal C}_n^{\mathrm H}=\prod_{j\in I}B_j\).  Let \(\widehat\theta_n^{\mathrm H}\) be the unique element of this product when it is a singleton and a fixed measurable element otherwise.  For \(n<2K\), define \(B_j=\{-1,+1\}\) and use the same fixed fallback.  This map uses only the \(d\) observable moment queries \(\psi_{ij}\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: This is the explicit data map attaining the unconditional chart frontier.

proposed.name: sub-half Hermite-chart exact-orientation sample complexity
proposed.construction:
\[
N_{\mathrm H}^*(d,\alpha,\lambda)=
\inf\left\{n:\inf_{\widetilde\theta}
\sup_{(P,\theta)\in\mathcal M_d^{\mathrm H}(\lambda)}
P^{\otimes n}(\widetilde\theta\ne\theta)\le\alpha\right\},
\]
where the inner infimum ranges over every measurable map from \((\mathbb R^{2d})^n\) to \(\{-1,+1\}^{I}\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The matched chart frontier must not overwrite the larger full-class functional, whose upper side remains unavailable.
After all three inference statements are rewired to the chart moment rule, this generated-residual rule has no live consumer and its required regression event is proved impossible.

proposed.statement:
Fix the sub-half Hermite chart selected in Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:subhalf\text{-}chart\text{-}calibration}\).  There are constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), depending only on this fixed chart and on the fixed Gaussian kernels, such that for every \(d\ge1\), \(0<\alpha\le1/4\), and \(0<\lambda\le\lambda_H\),
\[
n\lambda\ge C\log\frac{d+1}{\alpha}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\sup_{(P,\theta)\in\mathcal M_d^{\mathrm H}(\lambda)}
P^{\otimes n}(\widehat\theta_n^{\mathrm H}\ne\theta)\le\alpha/2,
\]
where \(\widehat\theta_n^{\mathrm H}\) is the explicit median-of-means rule in Definition \(\mathrm{def:chart\text{-}moment\text{-}rule}\).  Every measurable estimator has worst-case error greater than \(\alpha\) when \(n\lambda\le c\log((d+1)/\alpha)\).  Consequently,
\[
c\frac{\log((d+1)/\alpha)}{\lambda}
\le N_{\mathrm H}^*(d,\alpha,\lambda)
\le C\frac{\log((d+1)/\alpha)}{\lambda}.
\]
Since \(\mathcal M_d^{\mathrm H}(\lambda)\subset\mathcal M_d(\lambda)\), the same lower bound transfers to the full-class frontier \(N^*(d,\alpha,\lambda)\), but no full-class upper bound is asserted.
proposed.justification: The theorem is an unconditional matched all-procedure frontier on one explicit nonempty Hermite-chart class, with a fully specified observable estimator and the same mirror family on the converse side.
proposed.gap: Pointwise ANM consistency does not provide a local uniform \(\lambda^{-1}\log((d+1)/\alpha)\) exact-recovery theorem, and the former proposed local-polynomial route is proved infeasible.
proposed.consumer: Benchmark designers receive a valid sample-size law for simultaneous orientation on the declared chart, while being warned that it is not a full-class guarantee.

proposed.statement:
When \(d=1\), Definition \(\mathrm{def:chart\text{-}moment\text{-}rule}\) gives \(\widehat{\mathcal C}_n^{\mathrm H}=B_1\): it contains \(+1\) exactly when \(\widehat\mu_1+\rho_{n,1,\alpha}\ge0\) and contains \(-1\) exactly when \(\widehat\mu_1-\rho_{n,1,\alpha}\le0\).  On the sub-half chart the population sign of \(\mathbb E\psi(X_1,Y_1)\) equals the unique zero-residual-HSIC direction, and
\[
N_{\mathrm H}^*(1,\alpha,\lambda)\asymp
\lambda^{-1}\log(2/\alpha),
\qquad 0<\alpha\le1/4,\quad 0<\lambda\le\lambda_H.
\]

prose_updates.tldr: The headline has two honest parts. First, the explicit fixed local-polynomial nuisance protocol cannot satisfy its advertised simultaneous \(L^4\) event even for one legal positive-density Hermite-chart law, so the former conditional full-class upper and confidence theorems were vacuous. Second, after restricting to an explicit sub-half Hermite chart, the observable antisymmetric moment \(\psi(X,Y)=(X^2-1)Y-(Y^2-1)X\) has mean \(\theta\,2t(1-2a)\), bounded variance, and squared signal of order the wrong-direction residual-HSIC margin \(\lambda\). A median-of-means rule and product mirrors therefore give the unconditional matched frontier \(N_{\mathrm H}^*(d,\alpha,\lambda)\asymp\lambda^{-1}\log((d+1)/\alpha)\) and a computable simultaneous confidence set on that chart. The orientation-permuted attainable rectangle and the full-class product lower bound remain unconditional. The navigation score is GENE-inspired, not literally the published GENE score.

project_justification.gap: Published restricted-ANM results identify direction and regression--HSIC procedures have pointwise consistency, but neither supplies a uniform exact-recovery frontier for many supplied independent pairs. The attempted fixed local-polynomial route also concealed a genuine tail-design obstruction: its simultaneous \(L^4\) regression event fails inside the declared positive-density envelope.
project_justification.niche: The note separates feasible population geometry from statistical feasibility. Its explicit Hermite subchart is small enough to admit a computable nuisance-free orientation moment, yet rich enough to contain legal coordinate-swapped alternatives with residual-HSIC signal and testing information both of order \(\lambda\).
project_justification.fill: The feasible-image theorem supplies the local GENE-inspired-gain--HSIC rectangle. The new negative theorem closes the fixed local-polynomial kill test. On a calibrated interval \(0<a_-<a_+<1/2\), the antisymmetric moment gives a median-of-means estimator with simultaneous exponential error, while the same chart mirrors give the matching all-procedure lower bound and singleton obstruction. This proves the unconditional chart frontier without claiming a full-class upper bound. Wornbard et al. are credited for the non-archival presolve insight, not used as a theorem source.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The four-fold local-polynomial class \(\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{LP}}\) is retained only for the negative result: its declared simultaneous \(L^4\) event fails on a fixed legal chart law because a tail neighborhood is empty with nonvanishing probability. The unconditional chart estimator uses no fitted regression or residual-HSIC statistic; it evaluates one explicit antisymmetric moment per supplied pair and applies deterministic median-of-means blocks.

prose_updates.related_work: Li et al. (2025, Equation (6) and Theorem 4.3) motivate the navigation architecture, but their published GENE score uses neural-network \(R^2\) and a discretized chi-square independence-test indicator. The score here instead uses population explained variance and the oracle indicator \(\mathbf 1\{H>0\}\) for fixed characteristic Gaussian-kernel HSIC, so it is described only as GENE-inspired. Peters et al. (2014, Definition 27 and Theorem 28) provide the restricted positive-density identification domain; for a disjoint-edge DAG their multivariate condition reduces to the imposed pairwise Condition 19. Mooij et al. (2016, Appendix A) prove pointwise consistency of regression plus fixed-kernel HSIC under a suitable learner, not the uniform many-pair frontier here. Hl\'avka, Hu\v{s}kov\'a, and Meintanis (2011) emphasize that estimated residuals need a nuisance expansion; the present negative theorem shows that the particular fixed local-polynomial \(L^4\) event proposed here is impossible, without converting that failure into an HSIC-error rate. Shekhar, Kim, and Ramdas (2023), Kim, Balakrishnan, and Wasserman (2022), and Pfister et al. (2018) concern observed-variable or pointwise independence testing. Wang, Kolar, and Drton (2026) provide asymptotically valid ordering sets, while Gao and Stoev (2020) motivate exact simultaneous recovery transitions. Acharya et al. (2023) study a discrete interventional experiment and Jin (2026) studies linear LiNGAM primitive margins; neither is the nonlinear observational product experiment here. Wornbard et al. receive non-archival credit for the presolve geometry insight; no public theorem under that attribution is used.
prose_updates.interpretation: On the calibrated Hermite chart, residual HSIC remains the identifying population functional, while the antisymmetric moment is merely an observed-law estimating device whose sign is proved to equal the causal orientation. The GENE-inspired gain is used to define the feasible navigation window; it is not estimated by the chart rule and is not represented as the published GENE algorithm.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The matched upper bound is proved only on \(\mathcal M_d^{\mathrm H}(\lambda)\), the explicit sub-half Hermite-chart subclass. The local-polynomial theorem establishes failure of one prescribed uniform \(L^4\) nuisance event; it does not prove that residual HSIC is intrinsically hard to estimate, does not yield a nuisance-limited minimax bracket, and does not exclude a different full-class estimator. Consequently the full separated restricted-ANM class currently has the product lower bound but no matching upper bound.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Unconditional results are the attainable GENE-inspired-gain--HSIC rectangle, the fixed-protocol local-polynomial impossibility theorem, the product-testing lower bound, and the matched median-of-means frontier and confidence set on the explicit sub-half Hermite chart. The chart is a strict subclass of the note's independent-pair, unit-variance, weighted-Hölder, Gaussian-envelope, margin-window model, itself a strict subclass of Peters et al.'s corresponding restricted-ANM domain. A converse transfers upward through these inclusions; the chart achievability does not. No full-class upper frontier or generated-residual HSIC expansion is claimed.
